bib.title: High-Performance Large-Scale Image Recognition Without Normalization

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Brock, De, Smith, Simonyan (DeepMind), "High-Performance Large-Scale Image Recognition Without Normalization". The PDF is arXiv:2102.06171v1 (11 Feb 2021) and carries no ICML header, so the ICML 2021 venue comes from your brief, not from this file.
COVERAGE: Read all ~91,756 chars, pages 1–22, including Appendices A–E and Tables 1–6. I only skimmed the references.

CLAIMS
- claim: Batch norm has three main costs: compute and memory, a train/inference mismatch, and coupling between examples in a batch. Further costs follow from the coupling: it is hard to reproduce on other hardware, it causes bugs in distributed training, it leaks information in contrastive learning, it degrades when batch statistics vary a lot, and small batches hurt it.
  number: none
  setup: argued from prior work. Appendix B (p17) adds a Keras bug where BN statistics keep updating in test mode, DCGAN/SAGAN running BN in train mode at test time, and EfficientNet's cross-replica BN.
  quote: "batch normalization has three significant practical disadvantages... Third, and most importantly, batch normalization breaks the independence between training examples in the minibatch." / "batch normalized networks perform poorly when the batch size is too small (Hoffer et al., 2017; Ioffe, 2017; Wu & He, 2018)"
  where: p1–2
- claim: AGC clips each unit, meaning each row of a layer's gradient (fan-in for conv filters). It clips whenever the ratio of gradient norm to weight norm goes above λ. Smaller λ is needed at larger batch sizes, and the default is λ=0.01 for batch sizes 1024–4096.
  number: λ ∈ [0.01…0.16]; ε=10^-3; λ=0.01
  setup: NF-ResNet-50/200, ImageNet, SGD with Nesterov momentum, 90 epochs, LR 0.1×B/256. AGC is applied to every layer except the final linear layer.
  quote: "G𝓁i→ λ‖W𝓁i‖⋆F/‖G𝓁i‖F G𝓁i if ‖G𝓁i‖F/‖W𝓁i‖⋆F >λ" ; "Empirically, we find λ should be smaller for larger batches." ; "For batch size 1024 to 4096, set λ = 0.01"
  where: p4, p6
- claim: With AGC, NF-ResNets match or beat BN ResNets up to batch size 4096. Without AGC they fall behind BN at batch size 4096 and above. The text gives no exact accuracies for this ablation; they appear only in the Fig 2(a) plot.
  number: batch size 4096
  setup: NF-ResNet-50/200, batch sizes 256–4096. Each point is the mean of the best 4 of 5 runs, at the best λ for that batch size.
  quote: "they perform worse than batch normalized networks for large batch sizes (4096 or higher)" ; "AGC helps scale NF-ResNets to large batch sizes while maintaining performance comparable or better than batch-normalized networks on both ResNet50 and ResNet200. As anticipated, the benefits of using AGC are smaller when the batch size is small."
  where: p3, p4; p21
- claim: NFNet-F1 matches EfficientNet-B7's top-1 at 8.7× less training time per step. F5 reaches 86.0%, and F6+SAM reaches 86.5%.
  number: 84.7% top-1 each; latency 158.5ms vs 1397.0ms; 86.0%; 86.5%
  setup: ImageNet without extra data, single crop. Batch 4096, 360 epochs, averaged over 3 seeds. Latency is the median wall-clock time of one training step over 5000 steps, measured on 32 TPUv3 devices at batch 32 per device (bf16), with data loading excluded. These numbers measure training speed, not inference.
  quote: "NFNet-F1 model matches the 84.7% of EfficientNet-B7 with RA (Cubuk et al., 2020), while being 8.7 times faster to train"
  where: p8; Table 3 p7; A.2 p13–14
- claim: Swapping the NF setup for batch norm in the same architectures gives similar or slightly lower accuracy and makes training 20–40% slower. F4 and F5 would not train stably with BN.
  number: F0 83.6% at 73.3ms (NF) vs 83.4% at 111.7ms (BN)
  setup: Table 6, TPUv3. The authors blame bfloat16 numerics interacting with BN statistics.
  quote: "between 20% and 40% slower to train, even when using highly optimized batch normalization implementations without cross-replica syncing"
  where: p7–8, p19
- claim: After pre-training on JFT-300M and fine-tuning on ImageNet, NF-ResNets beat BN-ResNets by about 1% top-1, and NFNet-F4+ reaches 89.2%.
  number: ~1% (e.g. ResNet-50 at 384px: 81.1 vs 79.9); 89.2%
  setup: Pre-trained 10 epochs (ResNets) or 20 epochs (F4+). Fine-tuned 15k steps at batch 2048. Single seed. JFT is a private dataset.
  quote: "Normalizer-Free networks outperform their Batch-Normalized counterparts in every single case, typically by a margin of around 1% absolute top-1" ; "NFNet-F4+ attains an ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 89.2%"
  where: p8, Table 4–5 p8/p14, A.5 p15

LIMITS:
- The paper never shows exact accuracies with and without AGC; they exist only in Fig 2(a).
- The authors concede the best λ "may depend on the choice of optimizer, learning rate and batch size".
- NFNets need heavy explicit regularisation, otherwise they "dramatically overfit".
- They are not competitive on accuracy per parameter (F0 has 71.5M params vs 5.3M for EffNet-B0).
- They are tuned for training speed on TPU/GPU, and the paper reports no inference latency.
- Transfer results use one seed and a private dataset. 89.2% is beaten by Meta Pseudo Labels (90.2%).
- Image classification only, with no attention variants. Large batches do not beat small ones on accuracy at a fixed epoch budget.
- For your note: the paper does not cite Wu & Johnson. Its small-batch citation is Wu & He 2018 (Group Normalization).

BUILDS ON: Brock, De & Smith (ICLR 2021), the original NF-ResNets; De & Smith (NeurIPS 2020), SkipInit; Qiao et al. (2019 arXiv), Weight Standardization; Pascanu et al. (ICML 2013), gradient clipping; You et al. (2017 arXiv), LARS; Ioffe & Szegedy (ICML 2015), batch norm; Tan & Le (ICML 2019), EfficientNet; Foret et al. (ICLR 2021), SAM; Goyal et al. (2017 arXiv), linear LR scaling.

FIGURES: Fig 2, p4: "(a) AGC efficiently scales NF-ResNets to larger batch sizes. (b) The performance across different clipping thresholds λ." Panel (a) shows BN against NF with and without AGC across batch sizes in one view. Panel (b) shows the link between λ and batch size directly.

PROBLEMS: Equation layout was slightly garbled in extraction, but the formulas can be rebuilt. Plot values cannot be read as text. I found no instructions embedded in the text.
